# Native Integration Requirements Checklist: Agent Guard

**Purpose**: Review whether the written requirements define complete, consistent, and measurable native integration and compatibility commitments.
**Created**: 2026-09-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by `$speckit-checklist` from the active feature context.
**Review Ownership**: This is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines that the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means requirements quality was reviewed and satisfied; it does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the three promised native integrations named consistently, with no dependency on the separate demonstration application? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §FR-29]
- [x] CHK002 Are the protected input submission and final answer delivery boundaries defined for each supported integration arrangement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-01, Spec §FR-03, Spec §FR-04, Spec §AC-22]
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements explicit about rechecking assembled input after history, retrieval, or middleware changes it? [Completeness, Spec §FR-10, Spec §AC-03]
- [x] CHK004 Are direct answer and retrieval answer paths both included in every integration's final answer coverage? [Completeness, Spec §FR-05, Spec §AC-11, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK005 Are supported ordinary and asynchronous execution surfaces stated for each integration, including any integration that offers only an async native surface? [Completeness, Spec §FR-06, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK006 Are caller responsibilities for providing current request context, evidence identity, and final answer boundaries distinguished from adapter guarantees? [Completeness, Spec §FR-11, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is the meaning of an unchanged permitted native result clear for response form, metadata, and state effects? [Clarity, Spec §FR-02, Spec §AC-01]
- [x] CHK008 Is the distinction between a final answer and an intermediate tool request clear enough to prevent an integration from treating both as the same output boundary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-05, Spec §AC-11]
- [x] CHK009 Are the conditions for rejecting an identifiable unsupported arrangement distinguished from a documented limitation that the integration cannot observe? [Clarity, Spec §FR-26, Spec §AC-22]
- [x] CHK010 Is it clear which content forms and size limits an integration may accept, and whether the limits are product requirements or planning decisions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-19, Spec §FR-26, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK011 Is the boundary between an adapter failure, a guard evaluation failure, and a caller exception defined without converting caller failures into policy outcomes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-15, Spec §FR-25, Spec §AC-20]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK012 Do native integration requirements preserve the same required and optional policy decisions as the shared live and offline rules? [Consistency, Spec §FR-18, Spec §FR-20, Spec §AC-12]
- [x] CHK013 Are permitted result preservation and the prohibition on duplicate protected execution consistent across the user story, requirements, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §AC-01, Spec §FR-02, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK014 Are the spec's integration commitments consistent with the plan's claimed Python versions, framework surfaces, and optional dependency groups? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Project Structure]
- [x] CHK015 Are unsupported streaming and unobservable later mutations treated consistently in requirements, acceptance scenarios, and integration documentation commitments? [Consistency, Spec §FR-10, Spec §FR-26, Spec §AC-22]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK016 Can each integration's safe, input-blocked, and output-blocked outcomes be judged from written acceptance criteria without assuming a particular adapter design? [Measurability, Spec §AC-01, Spec §AC-02, Spec §AC-04, Spec §AC-23]
- [x] CHK017 Are the direct answer and retrieval answer acceptance conditions measurable separately for every promised integration? [Measurability, Spec §AC-11, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK018 Do acceptance criteria define what equivalent ordinary and asynchronous policy decisions mean when their native result forms differ? [Measurability, Spec §FR-06, Spec §AC-20]
- [x] CHK019 Are compatibility claims tied to an explicit evidence rule for the oldest and newest advertised dependency versions? [Measurability, Assumption, Constitution §Open Source and Compatibility]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Are alternate paths covered when retrieved content adds prohibited information after the initial request was checked? [Coverage, Spec §AC-03, Spec §FR-10]
- [x] CHK021 Are exception requirements written for cancellation and host application errors during guarded execution? [Coverage, Spec §FR-25, Spec §AC-20]
- [x] CHK022 Are concurrent requests with distinct policies and evidence covered as an integration requirement, rather than only as a core policy property? [Coverage, Spec §FR-25, Spec §AC-21]
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements clear when an output block follows an earlier tool action or state update, including the limits of rollback claims? [Coverage, Spec §FR-04, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK024 Are rejection requirements defined for identifiable streaming and unsupported integration arrangements before protected execution begins? [Coverage, Spec §FR-26, Spec §AC-22]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK025 Are optional integration dependencies and independence from unrelated integrations stated as release requirements rather than only a package layout proposal? [Completeness, Spec §FR-29, Plan §Project Structure]
- [x] CHK026 Are documented adoption instructions required to show a safe and blocked case for each promised integration without the demonstration application? [Completeness, Spec §AC-23, Spec §FR-29]
- [x] CHK027 Is the scope of claimed framework compatibility distinguished from versions selected for initial planning and versions actually supported by release evidence? [Clarity, Assumption, Spec §FR-29, Plan §Technical Context]

## Notes

- This checklist reviews written requirements, not the behavior of an SDK implementation.
- The focus is native integrations and compatibility at standard depth for a reviewer before implementation. The existing [security checklist](security.md) covers privacy and policy enforcement in detail.
- At checklist generation the workspace had a plan but no `tasks.md` or detailed contract files. The 2026-09-27 plan revision created the contract files; `tasks.md` remains for the task phase.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review. Leave items unchecked while they need clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- [requirements.md](requirements.md) has a separate built-in lifecycle under `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.

## Requirements Review — 2026-09-27

**Reviewer**: Codex, at the user's request. **Initial result**: 22/27 criteria satisfied by the written requirements before the follow-up amendment. Checked items assess requirements quality only; they do not certify implementation.

### Initial findings, resolved by the follow-up amendment

- **CHK002 — Per-integration boundaries**: FR-01–FR-05 define common boundaries, but the spec does not identify the native input and final-output boundary for each promised integration arrangement. The plan references an integration contract that is absent from this workspace.
- **CHK003 — Late input mutation**: FR-10 and AC-03 require assembled input coverage after history and retrieval additions. They do not say how a supported integration handles content that middleware changes after an earlier guard check, including whether a new check is required or the arrangement is unsupported.
- **CHK005 — Execution surfaces**: FR-06 promises ordinary and asynchronous use where supported. The plan identifies Microsoft Agent Framework as native async only, but neither artifact enumerates the supported native surfaces for LangChain and LangGraph.
- **CHK010 — Accepted content**: FR-19 and FR-26 require explicit failure for unsupported or oversized content. The plan gives numeric resource limits and excludes multimodal input, but the accepted native message/content forms per integration are not yet defined in an available artifact.
- **CHK011 — Adapter faults**: FR-15, FR-25, and AC-20 distinguish guard failures from caller errors and cancellation. They do not explicitly classify failures raised by an adapter while extracting native content or preserving native state.

**Initial review basis**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), and the [constitution](../../../.specify/memory/constitution.md). At the initial review, the plan listed detailed integration contracts that had not yet been created.

### Follow-up review — 2026-09-27

**Result**: 27/27 criteria satisfied by the amended written requirements. FR-31 and the Native Integration Coverage table define each framework's input, output, and execution surfaces (CHK002, CHK005). FR-32 and AC-33 define rechecking after content changes and rejection of known bypass arrangements (CHK003). FR-33 defines accepted text forms and context limits (CHK010). FR-34 and AC-34 distinguish configuration, runtime integration, policy evaluation, caller, and cancellation failures (CHK011). The subsequent plan revision created [integration contracts](../contracts/integrations.md); checked markers do not claim runtime compatibility evidence.
